transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep hearing voices at work—like from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They tell me which patient records have been changed. It sounds clear, like somebody is standing right next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it.
During this time, have you had a period of feeling unusually high or energized?

Yes. Some days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see what needs to be fixed at work and I’m supposed to handle it. But if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get really irritated and snap at them, like they’re getting in the way of something important.
Do you ever hear the voices when your mood feels normal—not unusually energized or irritable?

No, not really. I don’t remember hearing the call-light voices or seeing messages in the charts before I got so wound up about the rollout. It started after I was sleeping less and working nonstop, feeling like I had to fix everything there.
During these times, do you also feel unusually euphoric or on top of the world?

Yes, kind of. Some days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see exactly what needs to be fixed at work and I’m the one who’s supposed to handle it. It’s not just happy, though—I get really irritated if my husband or a nurse tells me to slow down, like they’re blocking something important.
Did there come a time when that unusually energized or irritable mood lasted for a full week or more?
Yes. It’s been more than a week—honestly, it’s been about two months now, since they asked me to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout.
Has there ever been a time when the voices continued for at least two weeks while your mood was not unusually high, energized, or irritable?

No, I don’t think so. The voices and the messages in the charts didn’t happen before I got so wound up with the rollout. They started after I was barely sleeping, working nonstop, and feeling like I had to fix everything at the facility.
During this period, have you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. My sleep hasn’t been normal, but I don’t know if I’d say I “needed” less sleep. I just know there have been nights where I didn’t sleep much, and I still kept going the next day.
